clue.text: Underground enthusiasts heading for certain states

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of the next word is used

parts.note: first letter of certain
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: Fans of something are on their way to some particular states of the union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underground enthusiasts' sounds like political dissidents; it means people who explore caves.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavers are hobbyists who explore caves, so they are literally enthusiasts below ground.

clue.text: I am turning up amongst a people not using English language

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to be amongst others is to sit in the middle of them
not using a letter means dropping it from the word

parts.note: a race is a people
E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the words read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A community that does not speak English has some new phrase rising among them.
explanation.walkthrough: A RACE loses its E to give ARAC, and the reversed I AM sits inside it: A-RA-MAI-C.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramaic is an ancient Semitic tongue, still spoken in a few communities, so it is a language.

clue.text: French are imprisoning the old observers

indicators.note: to imprison something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: tu es is French for you are
ye is an archaic form of the

explanation.surface: The French are locking up a bygone people.
explanation.walkthrough: ES is the French verb form in tu es; YE is the mock-antique spelling of 'the', as in Ye Olde Shoppe.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes are the organs that watch, so they are what does the observing.

clue.text: A few remain unsettled at heart in English county

parts.note: some means a few

indicators.note: only the middle of the word is disturbed, so its central letters swap places

parts.note: to rest is to remain

explanation.surface: Some people stay in an English county, uneasy deep down.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the two middle letters of REST, its heart, are rearranged, giving RSET. Somerset is a rural county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is one of the shires of south-west England, home of Cheddar and Glastonbury.

clue.text: Flowering plant's trouble: kept regressing

indicators.note: to regress is to go backwards, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: to ail is to trouble
had means kept, as in had it in a drawer

explanation.surface: A gardener's plant is in trouble: it keeps going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The dahlia is a garden plant prized for its large colourful blooms.

clue.text: No good blocking state payment for computer security item

indicators.note: something blocking a passage sits inside it, so one piece lies within the other

parts.note: the dole is unemployment benefit paid by the state
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: Something useless is holding up a benefit payment for a piece of IT kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole is the British name for state unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: A dongle is a small plug-in device that unlocks licensed software, acting as a security key.

clue.text: Vessel associated with a tower?

parts.note: surface reading: a ship linked to a castle keep or tall building
setter's reading: a tower is something that tows, here an animal pulling a barge along a canal towpath

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tower' is read as one who tows rather than a tall building, and the vessel is a barge pulled by an animal on the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseboat is a canal barge drawn by a horse walking the towpath, so its tower is the horse.

clue.text: One group of soldiers abandoning French city base

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: abandoning something means leaving it out, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: Grenoble is a city in the French Alps
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: A unit of troops leaves a French city to return to base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like a military camp to fit the soldiers; it is the adjective meaning low or dishonourable.
explanation.definitionFit: Base, as an adjective, means morally low or dishonourable, which is exactly what ignoble means.

clue.text: Mechanic and master at work

indicators.note: letters at work are busy being moved about and reorganised

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A garage mechanic and his boss are both busy at the workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mechanic and master' looks like two people; 'and master' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanic is a skilled manual worker, and tradesman is the general word for such a craftsman.

clue.text: Hurrying to arrest fool? It's very sad

indicators.note: to arrest someone is to hold them, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: tearing along means rushing
a jerk is a fool

explanation.surface: Police rushing to arrest an idiot: a sad sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A tear-jerking film or story is one sad enough to make the audience cry.

clue.text: Calls round to meet saint

parts.note: a ring is a round shape
S is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: Someone telephones to arrange a visit to a holy person.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring someone is to telephone them, so rings is a synonym of calls in that sense.

clue.text: Supporting environmental targets subject to law about pollution

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: suable means liable to be sued in court
a stain is a contamination or blot

explanation.surface: Green goals are backed by legislation on pollution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject to law' reads as legal regulation, but it is a rare adjective meaning open to being sued in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Sustainable describes practices that meet green goals by not depleting resources, so it supports environmental aims.

clue.text: Bede, perhaps, coming in to read a manuscript

indicators.note: the answer comes in to the following words, sitting inside them

parts.note: spans the end of read, the word a, and the start of manuscript

explanation.surface: The Venerable Bede arrives to study an old manuscript.
explanation.walkthrough: Bede suggests the medieval monk and historian; here it is the surname of George Eliot's hero in the novel Adam Bede.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam Bede is the title character of George Eliot's novel, so a Bede whose first name is Adam.

clue.text: Public transport lines filling routes by going all over the place

indicators.note: something filling another goes inside it
letters going all over the place are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A bus service takes chaotic routes to fill its lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A trolleybus is an electric bus fed by overhead wires, a form of public transport.

clue.text: Tried for better position Scotsman was observing

parts.note: Jock is a nickname for a Scotsman
eyed means watched

explanation.surface: A Scot was watching while someone angled for advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: To jockey for position is an idiom for manoeuvring to gain an advantage.

clue.text: Hide porn when getting treatment with new brain chemical

indicators.note: material that gets treatment is processed and reworked into another form

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Advice to conceal smut while undergoing therapy, alongside a new neurotransmitter.
explanation.definitionFit: Endorphins are hormones released in the brain that relieve pain and lift mood, so a neurochemical.

clue.text: US celebrity cancelling finale to include European art form

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside
cancelling the finale means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Oprah Winfrey, the American talk-show host
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: An American star drops the climax of her show to bring in some European culture.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera, drama set to music, is one of the classical performing arts.

clue.text: Endless inducement to imprison fascist leader is a healthy sign

indicators.note: to imprison is to hold inside, so one piece goes within the other
with no end, the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a cause is what induces something
Il Duce was Mussolini's title

explanation.surface: A bribe to jail a dictator would be a good omen.
explanation.definitionFit: The caduceus, a staff with twin snakes, is widely used as an emblem of medicine and health.

clue.text: Moved quickly — discovered with time to spare

indicators.note: to spare something is to do without it, so that letter goes

parts.note: traced means tracked down or found
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone hurried and found they had minutes in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With time to spare' reads as arriving early; it tells you to lose the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Raced means went at speed, so it is a synonym for moved quickly.

clue.text: Mad American's signal to bring in unruly pack

indicators.note: to bring something in is to take it inside

parts.note: a cue is a signal to act

indicators.note: an unruly group refuses to stay in order, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crazy American signals for a rowdy gang to be let in.
explanation.walkthrough: In US slang a cupcake can be an eccentric or crazy person, so 'Mad American' is the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupcake is American slang for an odd or crazy person, so it names a mad American.

clue.text: Irregular soldier's skill adopted by Italian city resident

indicators.note: something adopted is taken in, so it sits inside the other piece

parts.note: a Pisan lives in Pisa
art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A guerrilla's know-how is taken up by someone living in an Italian town.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a member of an armed resistance band, fighting outside a regular army.

clue.text: Range around US city, looking up, inducing fainting fit

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: scope means range or extent

indicators.note: in a down entry, looking up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: NY is New York

explanation.surface: Mountains around an American city, gazing upward, make a visitor swoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Syncope is the medical term for a temporary loss of consciousness, that is, fainting.

clue.text: Get rid of power in fuel with some energy extracted

indicators.note: something extracted is pulled out, so that letter is removed
in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: diesel is a fuel
P is the symbol for power
E is the symbol for energy; only one of the fuel's two is meant

explanation.surface: Banish the power in fuel once part of its energy has been drawn off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some energy' means just one E of the two in DIESEL: DISEL, then P goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispel is to drive away or banish, so it means get rid of.

clue.text: Irreverent about former monarch and very resistant to change?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around the others

parts.note: impious means lacking reverence
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late queen
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Disrespectful about the old queen and very set in their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'resistant to change' is a loose take on impervious, which strictly means letting nothing through.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impervious cannot be penetrated or affected, so it is unaltered by outside influence.

clue.text: Very good book about Newton — though I wouldn't think it would do for you!

definitions.text: though I wouldn't think it would do for you!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: so means very, as in so kind
B is the abbreviation for book
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: Praising a fine book about Isaac Newton, then sniffily adding it is not for you.
explanation.walkthrough: SO and B join, and N sits inside them. The definition is a quotation: what a person who looks down on others says.
explanation.definitionFit: A snob looks down on others' tastes, typically implying something is too good for them.

clue.text: Decoration, though denied second top award in pageantry

indicators.note: being denied something means going without it, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: a pompom is a decorative woolly ball
the OM, Order of Merit, is a top British honour; the second one in the word goes

explanation.surface: A medal is withheld for the runner-up at a grand ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' marks which OM goes: the one at the end. The Order of Merit is an elite honour given by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomp is splendid ceremonial display, which is what pageantry means.

clue.text: Understand husband will give up son in plot

indicators.note: one thing gives up its place for another, so one letter is swapped for a new one

parts.note: to grasp is to understand
H is the abbreviation for husband
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A husband realises he must give up his son as part of a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' sounds like a scheme; it is the verb meaning to chart on axes, or the noun for a chart.
explanation.definitionFit: A graph is a diagram of plotted points, and a plot is such a chart.

clue.text: Chemical secretion increasingly reflected in dial

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: to dial is to phone

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirrored, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: more and more means increasingly

explanation.surface: A chemical release shows up more and more on a meter's face.
explanation.definitionFit: A pheromone is a chemical secreted by an animal that affects the behaviour of others of its species.

clue.text: Sailors tucking into meat about the time things are developing

definitions.text: about the time things are developing

indicators.note: diners tucking into food go inside it, so one piece enters the other

parts.note: veal is calf meat
the RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Seamen eat meat when things are going well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' belongs to the definition, meaning concerning, not to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Vernal means relating to spring, the season when plants grow and new life develops.

clue.text: Meal excellent, with additional helping of one ingredient

indicators.note: an additional helping adds an extra portion within the dish

parts.note: super means excellent
one of the letters already in the word, served a second time

explanation.surface: An excellent dinner, with second helpings of one dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'ingredient' is one of the word's own letters: SUPER gets a second P.
explanation.definitionFit: Supper is the evening meal, so it is a kind of meal.
